request.spec:
Anyone using the app first signs in by typing a name; there is no password. The signed-in
name shows on the screen. A sheet is chosen by typing its id and loading it; the active sheet id
shows on the screen, and everything else in the app is kept per sheet. A sheet that has never been
loaded before starts empty. Everything happens on the one screen at /.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Anyone using the app first signs in by typing a name; there is no password. The signed-in
name shows on the screen. A sheet is chosen by typing its id and loading it; the active sheet id
shows on the screen, and everything else in the app is kept per sheet. A sheet that has never been
loaded before starts empty. Everything happens on the one screen at /.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Sign-in and sheet loading now work, and `bin/e2e` passes (1 test).

**Server**
- `V1__sheet.sql` adds a `sheet` table. A sheet is created, empty, the first time its id is loaded. That table is where everything else will be kept per sheet.
- `POST /api/signin` takes a name and checks it isn't blank. There is no password.
- `POST /api/sheets/{id}/load` returns the stored sheet, or creates it if the id is new. The signed-in name is sent in an `X-User` header. This follows the usual Spring layout: entity, repository, service and controller under `sheet/` and `session/`.

**Front end**
- A `Session` service (`core/session.ts`) holds the signed-in name and the active sheet id as signals.
- The home screen at `/` shows the sign-in form until someone signs in. After that it shows their name (`current-user`), a form to load a sheet by id (`sheet-id-input`, `sheet-load`) and the active sheet id (`sheet-current-id`).
- Each form has its own error element (`signin-error`, `sheet-load-error`). It appears when a blank name or id is submitted or the request fails, and clears as soon as the form is edited or submitted again.
- The existing `home-empty` test id stays on screen until a sheet is loaded, so it isn't removed.

One bug came up along the way: the first test run timed out after sign-in because the forms had no form group, so Angular never handled the submit and the browser reloaded the page instead. Switching both forms to a `FormGroup` fixed it.

Two things to be aware of:
- No audit records are written, because the test doesn't ask for any.
- Sign-in isn't kept on the server. The name lives in the browser and goes with each sheet request, so the server doesn't check who is calling.
